title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typed page (scanned upside down, headed 'n° 413, 1-41') is not about motives. It reads like a Bourbaki-style rédaction on Lie groups and appears to have been misfiled among the 1965 motive notes. The 'n° 413' numbering is consistent with Bourbaki's internal draft series, though this is an inference.

Setting: G is a Lie group of class C^r acting by a C^r law on a manifold X. U(G) is the algebra of point distributions supported at the identity e (the enveloping algebra), filtered by order: U^{(s)}(G) is the part of order ≤ s. ε_x is the Dirac mass at x, and T^{(s)}(X) is the bundle of point distributions (jets) of order ≤ s.

Step 1. For t in U^{(s)}(G), the convolution t*ε_x is pushed forward by the orbit map ρ(x): g ↦ gx. So x ↦ t*ε_x is a section of T^{(s)}(X), i.e. a differential operator L^X_t of order ≤ s. Concretely, (L_t φ)(x) = t(φ∘ρ(x)).

Step 2. L^X_t is of class C^{r-s}. The proof composes three facts:
- the constant map x ↦ t;
- the C^r section x ↦ ε_x;
- the bilinear bundle morphism (u,v) ↦ u*v from T^{(s)}(G) × T^{(0)}(X) to T^{(s)}(X), which is of class C^{r-s}.

Step 3. If t has no constant term, then L_t kills constants. For t a tangent vector at e, L_t is the fundamental vector field x ↦ tx. The resulting linear map T_e(G) → vector fields on X is the 'loi d'opération infinitésimale' (infinitesimal action).

Step 4 (Proposition 23). The map t ↦ L^X_t is linear. For s + s' ≤ r it satisfies L_{t'*t} = L_t ∘ L_{t'}, i.e. it is an anti-homomorphism for a left action. The proof begins on this page and is cut off. It completes as follows: (t'*t)(φ∘ρ(x)) = t_h t'_g φ(ghx) = t_h (L_{t'}φ)(hx) = L_t(L_{t'}φ)(x).

The purpose is the standard passage from a group action to an action of U(G) by differential operators (Lie's first theorem in distribution language).
errors: No mathematical errors. Proposition 23 is correct with the stated convention: left action, (L_tφ)(x) = t(φ∘ρ(x)), so the map is an anti-homomorphism.
Minor remark: the constant map x ↦ t is in fact smooth; calling it C^{r-s} only reflects the regularity of the manifold T^{(s)}(G).
The page is unrelated to the surrounding manuscript on motives over number fields and appears to be a misplaced sheet (possibly reused paper).

ideas.what: Point distributions of order ≤ s at the identity (U(G)) acting on a G-manifold X as differential operators via t*ε_x
ideas.modern_name: Action of the universal enveloping algebra by differential operators; distribution algebra of a Lie group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Lie, Cartan); this distribution formulation is Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, Ch. III §3 (1972)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Ch. III (distribution formalism); analogous algebraic version in SGA 3 Exp. VII

ideas.what: Infinitesimal action T_e(G) → vector fields on X, and the anti-homomorphism property L_{t'*t} = L_t ∘ L_{t'}
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki LIE III §3; for group schemes, SGA 3 Exp. II/VII

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard Bourbaki-style typescript on infinitesimal actions of Lie groups, apparently misfiled in the motives folder. The mathematics is textbook and was published in Bourbaki LIE III. The only curiosity is archival: a Bourbaki draft sheet in Grothendieck's motive notes.
transcription_corrections: The scanned page is upside down; the transcription correctly reads it rotated.
'Nous le noterons souvent L^X_t' should be read as 'L^X_t (or simply L_t)'. The last line uses L_{t'} without the superscript X, as on the page.
The page does not visibly define ρ(x) beyond its use. It is the orbit map g ↦ gx (presumably defined on an earlier page).
